Individuals typically reach reproductive maturity at a total length of 7.6 centimeters [Lp = 7.6 centimeters], a threshold that marks the onset of gonadal development and the transition from the juvenile phase. At the point of sexual maturation, individuals weigh roughly 2.9 grams [Wwp = roughly 2.9 grams], representing a substantial increase from neonatal mass but still far below the asymptotic adult size. These morphological benchmarks are essential for understanding the species' position within the broader life-history continuum of freshwater atherinopsids.

The high water temperature accelerates metabolic rates during these early developmental windows, compressing the timeframe available for the trophic switch from endogenous to exogenous nutrition.
